verifications.claim: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact date.

verifications.claim: The Challenger orbiter disintegrated 73 seconds after liftoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'broke apart 73 seconds into its flight'; R2: 'exploded 73 seconds after liftoff'; R3: 'disintegrated 73 seconds after launch'
verifications.reasoning: Exact timing directly supported by multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The disintegration killed all seven crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'killing all seven crew members'; R2: 'killing all seven crew members'; R3: 'killing all seven astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm seven crew members killed.

verifications.claim: A failed O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster caused the fatal structural failure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'failure of the primary and secondary O-ring seals in a joint in the right Space Shuttle Solid Rocket Booster (SRB)'; R2: 'O-ring seal failure in a rocket booster'; R3: 'O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster (SRB) failed'
verifications.reasoning: Direct attribution to right SRB O-ring failure in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Cold temperatures compromised the O-ring seal.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'record-low temperatures ... stiffened the rubber O-rings'; R2: 'worsened by cold weather'; R3: 'hardened the O-rings'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly link cold temperatures to O-ring compromise.

verifications.claim: The Challenger disaster forced a 32-month shutdown of the shuttle program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '32-month hiatus in the Space Shuttle program'
verifications.reasoning: Exact duration directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Challenger shuttle broke up at 11:38 a.m. EST.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launched ... at 11:38:00 a.m.' ... 'disintegrated ... at 16:39:13 UTC (11:39:13 a.m. EST)'
verifications.reasoning: Breakup was at 11:39:13 a.m. EST, 73 seconds after 11:38 launch; claim incorrectly states 11:38.

verifications.claim: The Challenger shuttle broke up 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about 46,000 feet (14 km) above the Atlantic Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Exact altitude and location directly supported.

verifications.claim: A cold-induced failure of the O-ring seal allowed hot gas to breach the solid rocket booster.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'cold temperature in the joint had prevented the O-rings from creating a seal ... hot gas was able to travel past the O-rings'; R3: 'hot propellant gases ... erode and then ‘blow by’ both the primary and secondary O-rings'
verifications.reasoning: Direct causal link described.

verifications.claim: The hot gas breach led to the rupture of the external fuel tank.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'burned through ... into the tank itself'; R2: 'ignited the main liquid fuel tank'
verifications.reasoning: Sequence of events directly matches.

verifications.claim: The seven Challenger crew members were Dick Scobee, Michael J. Smith, Ronald McNair, Ellison Onizuka, Judy Resnik, Greg Jarvis, and Christa McAuliffe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Dick Scobee ... Michael J. Smith ... Ronald McNair ... Ellison Onizuka ... Judith Resnik ... Gregory Jarvis ... Christa McAuliffe'; R2 and R6 list matching names/nicknames
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list with matching names/nicknames.

verifications.claim: The last known words from the Challenger crew came from pilot Michael J. Smith, who said "Uh oh."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pilot Mike Smith said "Uh-oh", which was the last crew comment recorded'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote and attribution confirmed.

verifications.claim: A comment from Commander Dick Scobee followed, which was cut off.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: Scobee's 'Roger, go at throttle up' at T+68 precedes Smith's 'Uh-oh' at T+72.284; no Scobee comment after 'Uh-oh'
verifications.reasoning: Sequence reversed; Scobee spoke before Smith, not after.

verifications.claim: The Challenger crew cabin was found in the ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crew compartment ... were recovered from the ocean floor'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of recovery.

verifications.claim: It is believed the Challenger astronauts died from the massive impact (over 200 mph) of the cabin with the ocean, rather than the initial explosion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'impact ... at 207 mph (333 km/h)'; 'several crew members are thought to have survived the initial breakup'; 'too violent to be survivable'
verifications.reasoning: Exact details on cause of death and speed match.

verifications.claim: The Challenger tragedy caused the US government to suspend the space shuttle program for over two years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '32-month hiatus' (over 2 years)
verifications.reasoning: 32 months exceeds two years; directly supported.

verifications.claim: The Rogers Commission identified the technical cause as the O-ring failure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The commission determined that the cause ... was hot gas blowing past the O-rings'
verifications.reasoning: Direct identification by commission.

verifications.claim: The Rogers Commission highlighted that NASA management ignored engineer warnings regarding the cold weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA managers also disregarded engineers' warnings about the dangers of launching in low temperatures'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in commission findings.

verifications.claim: Christa McAuliffe was the "teacher in space."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Teacher in Space Project'; R2: 'first teacher in space'; R3: 'teacher due to teach ... from space'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as such.

verifications.claim: Christa McAuliffe's lessons were performed in space in 2018.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention 2018 lessons; R1 notes project cancelled.

verifications.claim: A large segment of the Challenger was discovered on the ocean floor in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'November 10, 2022 ... a 20-foot (6 m) piece of the shuttle had been found ... on the ocean floor'
verifications.reasoning: Exact details match.

verifications.claim: There is an upcoming limited series about the Challenger mission starring Kristen Stewart as Sally Ride.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'limited series order ... The Challenger ... Kristen Stewart ... as Sally Ride'; R5: 'mini-series ‘The Challenger’ ... Kristen Stewart will play Sally Ride'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm series about Challenger (disaster/investigation) starring Stewart as Ride; 'mission' broadly fits context.

verifications.claim: The limited series is in development.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Amazon has officially greenlighted ... limited series order'; R5: 'Amazon finally greenlights mini-series'
verifications.reasoning: Greenlit status implies ongoing development; directly supported.
